findings: `PlaneCrossingTracker` still does not implement the frozen swept-volume test. It records vertex trajectories and triangle-edge intersections only at the interval endpoints; a rotating face can sweep across a rib between those endpoint configurations without any sampled point showing it. Therefore `clear_aperture` is not proven to have nonnegative signed distance from every rib (`task/run_screen_components_native_probe.py:269-316`; frozen requirement `artifacts/contract.json:194`).

The dynamic penetration metric is not the frozen signed-distance metric. It tests only mesh vertices lying within the floor slab and uses depth within that slab; it can miss face/edge penetration into ribs and does not measure the required dynamic-body pairs against screen, receiver, cup, table, media, and washer bodies (`task/run_screen_components_native_probe.py:493-504`; `artifacts/contract.json:93-100,188`).

The full-fixture penetration check samples only two underside lines above the support beams and derives receiver clearance from the receiver wall-top height. It does not compute signed distance over the complete screen floor, band, and wall geometry against receiver, supports, and table, so its passing aggregate cannot qualify `screen_fixture_signed_penetration_max` (`task/run_screen_components_native_probe.py:590-615,640-643`; `artifacts/contract.json:87-92,188`).

Bridge classification still uses the world-frame COM predicate `settled[2] > SCREEN_FLOOR_Z` instead of transforming the COM into the observed screen frame and testing screen-frame z > 0. This does not meet the frozen frame definition when the driven screen has residual translation or rotation (`task/run_screen_components_native_probe.py:514-519`; `artifacts/contract.json:200`).
